Make maps compatible and find overlap

How to

- Identify packages (st, tidyverse, tidycensus)
- give data information to AI
- tell it the goal
- Identify best function(s) for sf
- do a single censes tract to verify we are on track
- find a check

```{r}

# 1. Fetch census income data with geometry
oahu_income <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract", 
  variables = "B19013_001", 
  state = "HI", 
  county = "Honolulu", 
  geometry = TRUE, 
  year = 2022
) %>% 
  # Transform to local Oahu UTM projection (meters) for accurate spatial analysis
  st_transform(crs = 32604)

# 2. Load your solar panel GeoJSON data
# Replace "your_file.geojson" with your actual file name
solar_panels <- st_read(here("Data/oahu_solar_dedup_simple.geojson")) %>% 
  # Ensure the projection matches the census data exactly
  st_transform(crs = 32604) %>%
  st_make_valid() # Fixes any minor geometry/topology issues in polygon outlines

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SCENARIO A: If your GeoJSON contains POINTS (Counts per Tract)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
solar_points_joined <- st_join(solar_panels, oahu_income, join = st_intersects)

oahu_analysis_points <- oahu_income %>% 
  left_join(
    solar_points_joined %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      group_by(GEOID) %>% 
      summarise(solar_panel_count = n()),
    by = "GEOID"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(solar_panel_count = replace_na(solar_panel_count, 0))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SCENARIO B: If your GeoJSON contains POLYGONS (Area Overlap)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Intersect the physical shapes
solar_poly_intersect <- st_intersection(solar_panels, oahu_income) %>% 
  mutate(intersect_area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)))

oahu_analysis_poly <- oahu_income %>% 
  left_join(
    solar_poly_intersect %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      group_by(GEOID) %>% 
      summarise(solar_area_m2 = sum(intersect_area_m2)),
    by = "GEOID"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    solar_area_m2 = replace_na(solar_area_m2, 0),
    tract_area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)),
    pct_solar_coverage = (solar_area_m2 / tract_area_m2) * 100
  )

```

Points

```{r}
mapview(oahu_analysis_points, zcol = "estimate", layer.name = "Median Income") + 
  mapview(oahu_analysis_points, zcol = "solar_panel_count", layer.name = "Panel Count")

```

Area

```{r}
mapview(oahu_analysis_poly, zcol = "estimate", layer.name = "Median Income") + 
  mapview(oahu_analysis_poly, zcol = "pct_solar_coverage", layer.name = "% Solar Coverage")

```

Statistical test

```{r}
# 1. Fetch census income data
oahu_income <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract", 
  variables = "B19013_001", 
  state = "HI", 
  county = "Honolulu", 
  geometry = TRUE, 
  year = 2022
) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 32604) # Project to UTM Zone 4N (meters)

# 2. Load the GeoJSON polygons using here()
solar_polygons <- st_read(here("Data/oahu_solar_dedup_simple.geojson")) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 32604) %>% 
  st_make_valid() # Fixes any minor geometry/topology issues in polygon outlines

# 3. Calculate spatial overlap area
solar_intersect <- st_intersection(solar_polygons, oahu_income) %>% 
  mutate(intersect_area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)))

# 4. Aggregate overlap data back to the census tract level
oahu_analysis <- oahu_income %>% 
  left_join(
    solar_intersect %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      group_by(GEOID) %>% 
      summarise(solar_area_m2 = sum(intersect_area_m2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = "GEOID"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    solar_area_m2 = replace_na(solar_area_m2, 0),
    tract_area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)),
    # Metric 1: Percentage of the entire census tract covered by solar
    pct_solar_coverage = (solar_area_m2 / tract_area_m2) * 100
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. STATISTICAL CORRELATION TEST
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Filter out tracts where median income is missing (NA)
correlation_data <- oahu_analysis %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  filter(!is.na(estimate))

# Run a Spearman correlation (robust to outliers and skewed spatial data)
cor_test_result <- cor.test(
  correlation_data$estimate, 
  correlation_data$pct_solar_coverage, 
  method = "spearman"
)

# Print the statistical results
print(cor_test_result)

```
